fi-0gr5.title: Google car: Gen 3 snow only in the far northwest
fi-0gr5.summary: Snow in older Gen 3 coverage only exists in the far northwest. Snow in Gen 2, Gen 4 and trekker coverage can be elsewhere.

fi-601H.title: Road lines: edge lines always solid white
fi-601H.summary: Where there are edge lines, they are always solid white. Sweden and Norway use dashed edge lines. Only the Åland islands in the southwest use dashes.

differs.how: Sweden uses dashed edge lines
Norway uses dashed edge lines
Åland uses dashed edge lines

fi-6M6z.title: Bus stop: white plate with four numbers
fi-6M6z.summary: Bus stops show a white plate with 4 numbers, sometimes with a semicircle sign on top. Some stops in the main town don't follow this.

fi-6iou.title: Sign: solid blue direction sign, white border
fi-6iou.summary: Direction signs are solid blue with white text and a white border, with arrows.

fi-7DPm.title: Pole: orange snow pole, thin white band at top
fi-7DPm.summary: Orange snow poles with one thin white band near the top. Norway and Sweden have them too, but with a much wider white band lower down, sometimes several bands.

differs.how: wider white band, lower, sometimes several bands
wider white band, lower, sometimes several bands

fi-8fWv.title: Pole: simple wooden poles, often with a street light
fi-8fWv.summary: Mostly wooden utility poles with simple designs but various tops, often with a street light attached. Sweden, Norway and Estonia use wooden poles too.

fi-9y8k.title: Street sign: black border, all capitals
fi-9y8k.summary: Signs with a black border and all capital letters are almost only used by one city. Another city uses a similar one with a thicker, more compact font.

fi-9yCi.title: Buses: blue bottom, white top, NYSSE
fi-9yCi.summary: Buses are blue on the bottom and white on top, with the word NYSSE on the sides.

fi-A2lU.title: Sign: blue and white striped signposts
fi-A2lU.summary: Signposts often have blue and white stripes. Sweden has this too. Estonia has the same colours, but its stripes are wider and attached more loosely.

differs.how: stripes wider, attached looser to the post

fi-APDJ.title: Street sign: blue with white text
fi-APDJ.summary: Blue street signs with white text are unique to two towns in the west, one of them Seinäjoki, southeast of Vaasa.

fi-Aq7N.title: Pole: snow pole with two long reflectors
fi-Aq7N.summary: Snow poles with two long reflectors are on bigger roads in the far north, only in coverage from 2023 on.

fi-D09g.title: Google car: low-quality brownish camera, wide round blur
fi-D09g.summary: A rough older camera with a wide round car blur, no halo in the sky, and often brownish colours. Rare on good maps. Spain also has a lot of it, and unofficial coverage is common here.

differs.how: also has much coverage with this camera

fi-EIZt.title: Road lines: red-tinted road, dashed edge lines
fi-EIZt.summary: Roads have a reddish tint and dashed edge lines like Sweden's, both unlike the rest of the country.

differs.how: Swedish roads lack the red tint

fi-JnNg.title: Sign: pedestrian sign with 4 stripes
fi-JnNg.summary: Some pedestrian signs have 4 stripes, exactly like Sweden's. Many are still the normal 5-stripe design.

fi-KbXf.title: Landscape: hilly, low plants near mountains
fi-KbXf.summary: Close to the Scandinavian Mountains the land is hilly with low plants. The Gen 2 coverage was filmed in spring, so plants look dead.

fi-LRoW.title: Pole: lamp bolted twice at the very top
fi-LRoW.summary: Lamps on wooden poles are mounted on top with a double bolt and a straight arm. Sweden also double-bolts, but lower down and usually with curved arms.

differs.how: lamps lower on pole, arms usually not straight

fi-M4BM.title: Google car: low-mounted camera, big round blur
fi-M4BM.summary: A Gen 4 camera mounted lower than normal, with a fairly big round blur and a small bump at the front. The blur can be see-through, which makes it hard to spot. All Northern Europe has it.

fi-QWP9.title: Google car: Gen 3 with no antenna
fi-QWP9.summary: Older Gen 3 coverage with no antenna at all is found in south-central areas.

fi-RM0Y.title: Landmark: wind turbines along west coast
fi-RM0Y.summary: Wind turbines are mostly along the west coast, with some exceptions.

fi-RwDU.title: Plate: short, almost fully white, no blue strip
fi-RwDU.summary: White plates with blue text that look almost completely white on Street View. They are short and have no European blue strip.

fi-T6ca.title: Language: Sámi place names, letter c
fi-T6ca.summary: In the far north some signs show place names in both Finnish and Sámi. Sámi uses the letter c, which Finnish normally doesn't.

fi-VWG8.title: Street sign: blue and grey coat of arms
fi-VWG8.summary: Street signs with a blue and grey coat of arms in the top-left, and the neighbourhood name above the street name, mean one small southern city.

fi-XM2x.title: Sign: thin yellow edge on red-border signs
fi-XM2x.summary: Traffic signs with a red border have a thin yellow stroke on the very edge. No other Nordic country has this.

fi-YC5h.title: Landscape: lakes everywhere
fi-YC5h.summary: Lakes are so common that you rarely drive far without seeing water. The country is known as the Land of a Thousand Lakes.

fi-a1ax.title: Sign: pedestrian sign with 5 stripes
fi-a1ax.summary: The pedestrian sign has 5 stripes. Sweden and Norway usually have 4, though Norway rarely has 5.

differs.how: usually 4 stripes
usually 4 stripes, rarely 5

fi-b3ID.title: Google car: slightly tilted long antenna
fi-b3ID.summary: A long antenna that leans slightly, found in the southwest. Don't mix it up with the straight long antenna.

fi-b6ga.title: Language: long words, double vowels, ä and ö
fi-b6ga.summary: Unrelated to most European languages, with many long words and double vowels, and the letters ä and ö. Estonian looks similar but uses õ and ü, which Finnish lacks.

fi-bayT.title: Trams: green and yellow
fi-bayT.summary: Green and yellow trams. Only one other city has trams, and those are red.

fi-cjgP.title: Bollard: black and white, long, diagonal stripe
fi-cjgP.summary: Long black and white bollards with a rectangular white reflector on the front and two dots on the back. Round or thin and curved, with a usually diagonal black stripe. Other Nordic bollards look similar.

fi-dnPB.title: Shops: K-Market and S-Market
fi-dnPB.summary: K-Market (also K-Supermarket or K-Citymarket) and S-Market are supermarket chains with recognisable logos, found only here.

fi-dvdW.title: Street sign: white with black text, ends in tie or katu
fi-dvdW.summary: Street names mostly end in 'tie' (road) or 'katu' (street), on white signs with black text. 'Polku' and 'kuja' also appear.

fi-eAl2.title: Road: river valley, small stunted birch
fi-eAl2.summary: A far-northern road on the Norway border runs through a river valley with hills on both sides, a river often to the northwest and small stunted birch trees. Its Gen 3 coverage is autumn, so trees look bare.

differs.how: border road, use plates and signs to separate

fi-gI6b.title: Google car: Gen 3 coverage in autumn colours
fi-gI6b.summary: A lot of the older Gen 3 coverage was filmed in autumn, so trees show fall colours. This is much rarer in the other Nordic countries, so a fall look favours Finland. Not true for Gen 2 and Gen 4.

fi-grQV.title: Buses: yellow with white rear
fi-grQV.summary: Yellow buses with a white rear are unique to one southwestern city.

fi-hD3w.title: Houses: modern concrete blocks, wooden houses
fi-hD3w.summary: Mostly modern, practical buildings. Downtowns have concrete apartment blocks, and suburbs have single family homes, many with wooden cladding. Some country houses are painted dark red, like in Sweden and Norway.

fi-jfJU.title: Chevron: black with yellow arrows
fi-jfJU.summary: Chevrons are black with yellow arrows. Norway and Iceland use similar colours, but Sweden has blue and yellow ones.

differs.how: Swedish chevrons are blue and yellow

fi-ju7h.title: Location: island group off the southwest coast
fi-ju7h.summary: A self-governing island group with its own flag, off the southwest coast. It counts as Finland for streaks. It has no Gen 4 coverage.

differs.how: own flag, Swedish only, short plates, dashed edge lines

fi-lUjp.title: Plate: short white, blue strip
fi-lUjp.summary: Shorter than normal white plates with the usual blue strip on the left.

differs.how: Åland plates are short, fully white, no blue strip

fi-lm-2991.title: Sign: 5-stripe pedestrian sign, one arm up
fi-lm-2991.summary: A detailed man without a hat and 5 zebra stripes. The bold simple figure has one arm pointing up, unlike Denmark's.

differs.how: Danish figure has arms pointing down

fi-lm-3337.title: Buses: pink Jouko brand
fi-lm-3337.summary: Pink buses of the Jouko brand mean the south-eastern city of Lappeenranta.

fi-lm-3338.title: Buses: LSL company
fi-lm-3338.summary: Buses run by a company called LSL mean the city of Lahti.

fi-lm-3339.title: Buses: Vilkku company
fi-lm-3339.summary: Buses run by a company called Vilkku mean the city of Kuopio.

fi-lm-783086.title: Street sign: both -tie and -vägen
fi-lm-783086.summary: In coastal parts of the south and west, signs are bilingual: both -tie and -vägen (road), or -katu and -gatan (street). Swedish alone is also spoken on the island group in the southwest.

differs.how: Swedish signs never have the Finnish word beside it

fi-lvu5.title: Route marker: first digit of 3-4 digit road number
fi-lvu5.summary: On roads with 3 or 4 digits, the first digit shows the region, from 1 in the south to 9 in the north. Major 2-digit roads don't follow this.

fi-m9yR.title: Buses: pink front
fi-m9yR.summary: Buses have a pink front in one northern city.

fi-moyz.title: Buses: almost fully green
fi-moyz.summary: Buses are almost completely green in one central city.

fi-myrR.title: Landscape: farmland near west and south coast
fi-myrR.summary: There is a lot of farmland, but mostly near the west and south coasts.

fi-n3ab.title: Sign: yellow background road signs
fi-n3ab.summary: Road signs have a yellow background. Sweden and Iceland do too, but Norway's are white.

differs.how: Norwegian signs have a white background

fi-ndHC.title: Street sign: blue and yellow coat of arms
fi-ndHC.summary: Street signs with a blue and yellow coat of arms in the top-left corner mean one small southern city.

fi-oIBv.title: Plate: red metal plate with 7 golden bumps
fi-oIBv.summary: Red rectangular metal plates with 7 golden or dark red bumps forming a rounded hexagon on houses, lamp posts and signposts.

fi-p7Kd.title: Road lines: white dashes or yellow centre lines
fi-p7Kd.summary: Centre lines can be white dashes (with or without a solid line), solid yellow with white dashes, or double yellow. Yellow is being phased out. Sweden never has yellow centre lines.

differs.how: never has yellow centre lines
centre lines have an orange tint

fi-rc3m.title: Plants: small, stunted spindly trees
fi-rc3m.summary: Small stunted trees with thin spindly trunks are common in the north.

fi-stY3.title: Language: only Swedish, no Finnish
fi-stY3.summary: If you see only Swedish and no Finnish but suspect Finland, think of the small island group in the southwest.

fi-tLs3.title: Buses: blue and white, vertical split
fi-tLs3.summary: Buses in and around the capital are blue and white with a vertical split. Other places can have the same colours, so look for the transport company logo.

fi-u8ow.title: Google car: Gen 4 sidewalk trekkers
fi-u8ow.summary: The capital's downtown has a lot of Gen 4 walking-trekker coverage. Gen 3 walking trekkers exist in many other cities.

fi-wdcQ.title: Landscape: dense forest of pine and birch
fi-wdcQ.summary: Dense boreal forest. Pines are common, plus birches with white trunks.

fi-zivD.title: Language: Swedish text on south and west coasts
fi-zivD.summary: Swedish is common on some south and west coasts, often alongside Finnish. If you see Swedish in a Finnish-looking place, don't guess inland.

fi-zktw.title: Sign: only two kinds of bus stop sign
fi-zktw.summary: Only two bus stop sign styles: blue and white, or yellow and black. Sweden has many types, mostly with stop names written on them.

differs.how: many bus stop styles, most with stop names
